title: Repeated input labels raised the local phase null among 35 inputs to one leech motor neuron
abstract: We tested how repeated input labels affect a local contact-pair phase score in linked anatomy and voltage imaging from one leech ganglion. Among 35 mapped inputs to motor neuron DE-3R, 216 of 346 contact pairs within a 10 micrometre path distance came from the same input. We derived exact shuffle expectations and tested them by simulation. The mean score in two swim trials was 0.64715. Its whole-input shuffle expectation was 0.65685, with one-sided p = 0.52855. A contact shuffle had expectation 0.07632 and p = 0.00005, but broke the repeated-label structure. The two exact null means differed by 0.58053. A 21-input confidence check gave the same qualitative result. This is a diagnostic for site-based activity analysis, not a test of the source paper's cluster algorithm. One animal, selected inputs, uncertain matches, and missing raw phase errors limit biological inference. We provide code, exact formulas, derived tables, null draws, source hashes, a figure, and independent checks.

display.caption: Local contact identity and exact phase nulls in one leech motor neuron. Null draws are references, not animal confidence intervals.
